body:
Blackstone is lining up a $1 billion private-debt package to fund a proposed tie-up between Leidos’ security enterprise solutions units and Analogic, Bloomberg reported Monday.

Blackstone Credit & Insurance, a private-lending arm of alternative-asset manager Blackstone, is leading the financing alongside HPS Investment Partners, a credit manager, and banks Bank of America and Wells Fargo, Bloomberg said. The idea is to back a combination that pairs Leidos’ security enterprise solutions operations with Analogic’s imaging and detection technology used in areas like aviation screening and industrial automation. What’s notable is the funding route:..

route: instead of relying mainly on a widely sold leveraged loan, a small group of lenders can commit the money directly, negotiate borrower protections (the rules lenders set for the company), and reduce the risk that financing falls apart during syndication. That speed and certainty can matter for carve-outs and specialist assets, especially in defense-adjacent and security tech where revenues are often linked to government and critical-infrastructure spending.

Large M&A financings are increasingly being struck as private-credit “club deals”, where a handful of lenders set terms and hold more of the debt themselves. If this approach keeps spreading, Bank of America and Wells Fargo may lean more on partnering with direct lenders – using their balance sheets selectively and earning fees – while a bigger share of leveraged-finance activity shifts away from the syndicated loan market. That can change where price discovery happens, who gets access to these loans, and how quickly deals can get done.
